output.summary: The release slip is explained by the single-reviewer AppSec gate. Queue depth and wait times grew while reviewer throughput stayed flat at about 4.4 reviews a week. Only the QA-to-sign-off stage lengthened (37 days), and squad-controlled stages did not change. During the August delegate cover the queue fell and six releases shipped. Non-gated Reporting patch releases kept a 14-day cadence. Engineer output, technical-debt measures and CI health are flat, so discipline and tech-debt explanations are contradicted. The idle tickets are mostly awaiting security review. The morale decline looks like a consequence of the wait, not a cause. Add review capacity (A1). Do not suspend the gate or cut scope before review outcomes and defect data (Q1, Q2) exist. The accountability program would be harmful.
